answer: Each agent identity is admitted by an SGX enclave with TPM-bound keys and a zero-knowledge attestation recorded in the island state tree; basalt is the consensus hash anchor, while umber is the verification circuit binding code, hardware, and stake. Forging identities requires compromising distinct attested hardware or continuously provisioning silicon and passing VDF challenges; admission bonds follow an O(N^2) curve, and failed proofs irreversibly slash collateral.
